newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks close up 2.84 pct on fund, exports.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks close up 2.84 pct on fund, exports.

text.p: Thai stocks closed 2.84 percent higher on Monday as investors welcomed a government announcement of a 50 billion baht support fund to help shore up the market, brokers said.
"I think the market support fund helped boost market sentiment. Comments by the central bank governor on improved March exports also lifted the market," said Samart Rusmeerojwong of James Capel Asia.
The composite SET index advanced 15.91 points to 577.10 on 4.09 billion baht turnover.

The market rallied for the second consecutive session. Sentiment improved after Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan said on Saturday that Thai commercial banks volunteered to pool the fund to help shore up the market which tumbled to near eight-year lows last week.
"I think the sharp rise today would be short-term as investors, especially foreigners, are watching how the support fund would work while economic worries are left unattended," Samart said.
Brokers said comments by Bank of Thailand Governor Rerngchai Marakanond shortly before the market close further helped stocks after their 15 percent plunge in the first half of May.

Rerngchai said Thai exports rose 4.8 percent year on year in March and averaged 4.4 percent growth during the first four months. He said his preliminary export figures were based on foreign exchange transactions that local exporters and importers conducted through the central bank.
The SET-50 index gained 1.48 points to 42.14.
Gainers led decliners 256 to 91 with 50 issues finishing unchanged.
Most sectors, except commerce, gained on Monday. Banks led the rally, rising 4.39 percent, the communication sector surged 2.85 percent, and the finance sector rose 6.39 percent.
Bangkok Bank topped the active list, advancing three baht to 150, Shinawatra Computer gained nine to 117, and Loxley retreated 2.75 to 46.
The market will be closed on Tuesday on a Buddhist religious holiday.
